title: Fan-apex test references node id 8, which is never spawned (setup only creates ids 0-5); also uses wrong port_capacity for the rim
evidence:
+		rim := puck_rim_world(&v, 4)
+		rs, _ := pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 8)
+		nw := node_world(&s.topology, rs, 26.0)
...vs setup: +	host := pp.topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, host_idx, {18, 16}, cat) // id 5  (last spawned id) and +	rt_idx, _ := pp.node_type_index(cat, "router_mid") // 8 ports (the 6-pipe fan fits)
detail: Node id 8 does not exist; node_slot fails and rs falls back to 0, so the assertion passes by accident. Rim is computed with port_capacity 4 though the router is router_mid (8 ports), weakening the check.
recommended_fix: Use pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 0) for the router and puck_rim_world(&v, 8) (or the catalog's port_capacity); assert the node_slot ok value so the test fails loudly on bad ids.

title: Spec contradicts itself on the golden re-bless: Code Map and Verification demand a re-bless while the verdict says NO re-bless
evidence:
+- `goldens/*` -- full deliberate T2 re-bless (cause-documented); T1 + replay byte-identical
+- [x] `goldens` -- VERDICT C: no re-bless needed (shipped flags off -> byte-identical T2) -- full deliberate T2 re-bless; T1/log.bin byte-identical (prove zero non-png diffs)
+- `tools/harness.sh run` -- all demos green after the re-bless; `git status goldens` shows ONLY .png diffs (T1/log.bin untouched)
detail: Same file says 'full deliberate T2 re-bless' and 'no re-bless needed' in one task line, and Verification still instructs checking for .png diffs from a re-bless that per the verdict never happened and must never happen.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the Code Map goldens line, the goldens task, and the Verification section to state the shipped truth: zero golden changes, no re-bless, harness proves byte-identity.

title: Frozen Intent promises anchors 'aligned to the incident directions' but the code allocates a rotated regular template independent of each pipe's actual direction
evidence:
+- Anchor allocation: at a router, n incident pipes get n anchors evenly spread around the puck, aligned to the incident directions (deterministic, snapped to the pinned CIRCLE16 table — no transcendentals in the rasterized path, §10.4).
...vs code: +	return (base + int(f32(rank) * 16.0 / f32(n) + 0.5)) % 16
detail: Anchors sit at base + rank*16/n on the 16-gon, where base is the mean incident direction. For asymmetric layouts the anchors do not align to the pipes' actual directions, contradicting the frozen spec text.
recommended_fix: Either snap each pipe's anchor to its own direction16 index (resolving collisions deterministically) or amend the spec wording to 'even template anchored at the mean direction'.

title: Assist glow recomputes wire paths per edge instead of sharing the frame's threaded paths slice like every other consumer
evidence:
+		path: Wire_Path
+		if v.route_wires {
+			band_w := band_world(v, bundles.bundle_tier[bi], int(bundles.bundle_count[bi]))
+			path = wire_path_compute(v, topo, bundles, bi, band_w)
...vs view.odin: +	// 7.5: the DRAWN wire paths — computed once per frame ONLY when a wire
detail: draw_world claims paths are computed once per frame and threaded, and crisis/selection/packets receive paths[:]. draw_glow_edge instead re-runs wire_path_compute (full detour scan) per glow edge — wasted work and a divergent code path.
recommended_fix: Thread the paths slice into draw_glow_edge like draw_crisis_outlines and index paths[bi]; fall back to wire_path_straight between apexes when absent.

title: test_degradation_straight_fallback never forces a degradation scenario; its ratio assertion is conditional and can pass vacuously
evidence:
+	// whatever the routing decided, the path must be valid + bounded
+	testing.expectf(t, p.n >= 2 && p.n <= MAX_WIRE_POINTS, "path n=%d out of bounds", p.n)
...
+	if p.n > 2 {
+		drawn := path_len(&p)
+		testing.expectf(t, drawn <= logical * WIRE_DETOUR_MAX_LEN_RATIO + 0.01,
detail: Named 'straight_fallback' but constructs no over-ratio or over-bend scenario; if the path returns straight, the only real degradation assertion is skipped. The spec's degradation acceptance criterion is effectively unpinned.
recommended_fix: Build a topology whose detour provably exceeds WIRE_DETOUR_MAX_LEN_RATIO (or exhausts WIRE_DETOUR_MAX_BENDS) and assert the returned path is exactly the 2-point straight fallback.

title: bundle_end_anchors discards its `end` parameter (`_ = end`) and then immediately branches on it
detail: The `_ = end` discard is a leftover no-op directly contradicted by the `if end == 0` three lines later. Harmless but signals an unfinished edit. Same smell: `_ = b` in test_cost_stays_on_logical_length after b is used.
recommended_fix: Delete the `_ = end` line (and the redundant `_ = b` in the test); the parameters are genuinely used.

title: Anchor.idx is written at every append site but never read anywhere in the diff
evidence:
+Anchor :: struct {
+	pos:  rl.Vector2,
+	idx:  int,
+	tier: u16,
+}
...writes: +	append(&out, Anchor{pos = nw + u * foot, idx = direction16(u.x, u.y), tier = bundles.bundle_tier[bi]})
...consumers: +			stub_w := band_world(v, anc.tier, 1) * 0.6 // the member's own narrow read
+			draw_fan_stub(v, anc.pos, apex_a, stub_w, tier_pipe_color(v, anc.tier))
detail: end_apex and the fan-stub loop read only anc.pos and anc.tier. The idx field is dead weight carried through every anchor; either consume it (debug/verification) or drop it.
recommended_fix: Remove idx from Anchor, or use it in a test/assertion that verifies anchors land on the intended 16-gon steps.

detail: The r2 additions (fan_estate_*, closeup_*_straight, *_anchors frames) were appended without updating the Emits list, so the file's own documentation describes half its output.

title: The flags-off branch in draw_bundles copy-pastes the entire lane-stripe and congestion-halo block, creating two parallel implementations to maintain
evidence:
+		if !v.route_wires && !v.wire_anchors {
+			ux, uy := dx / len_, dy / len_
+			nx, ny := -uy, ux // unit normal (one consistent side)
...
+			gutter := lane_gutter(v)
+			inner := band - 2*gutter*v.scale
+			bands := lane_bands(caps, inner)
...(the same gutter/inner/bands/lane_cols/halo logic exists again below for the variant path)
detail: To keep the legacy render byte-identical the pre-7.5 code was duplicated verbatim alongside the variant path. Any future fix to lane compositing or the halo must be applied twice; drift is inevitable.
recommended_fix: Factor the shared lane-compositing/halo color math into helpers parameterized by a polyline (straight 2-point path for legacy), so one implementation serves both branches.

title: draw_bundles requires a paths argument with no default while draw_packets/draw_selection/draw_crisis_outlines all default paths to nil
detail: Four consumers of the same paths slice, three with `= nil` defaults and one without. Inconsistent call contract for no evident reason; any secondary caller of draw_bundles must pass an explicit empty slice.
recommended_fix: Give draw_bundles the same `paths: []Wire_Path = nil` default as its sibling consumers.
